teaser.text: Keysight Technologies sells software, instruments, and network-testing systems that help engineers design electronics and prove that they work. Its dollar comes in mainly through those products and services, then goes out through research, production, selling, delivery, and support.

blocks.heading: Where could Keysight Technologies’s shares go?

paragraphs.text: The first weighted target is $256.81 per share in October 2027. That is a 22% loss. The final weighted target is $305.01 per share in October 2029. That is an 8% loss. The bear and bull cases each carry 25%; the base case carries 50%.

The October 2026 quarter tests the guide as supply constraints ease. Orders and book-to-bill—orders received divided by revenue—will show whether AI and optical demand, meaning demand for data carried as light through fiber connections, converts into shipments. A $700 million debt maturity in 2027, acquisition cash returns, and continued R&D investment will shape flexibility. Keysight’s value depends on AI and optical orders becoming delivered sales and cash.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for Keysight Technologies?

paragraphs.text: The bear case starts at $1,278M and falls to $1,072M in October 2028. It recovers to $1,296M by the final date because AI demand may cool, components may delay shipments and several end markets may weaken together. The bull case starts at $1,823M, reaches $2,139M, and ends at $2,468M as orders convert into deliveries and optical and software products improve mix. Q3 orders of $2.091B exceeded revenue of $1.846B, supporting that possibility.
The base case receives 50% because it requires fewer linked assumptions: FY2026 growth converts into shipments, margins normalize near the historical average and demand remains diversified.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Keysight Technologies really make?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow begins with cash from operations after capital spending. It is useful because it shows what the business produces after maintaining its equipment, but it is not automatically cash available to owners. Acquisitions, debt payments, repurchases, and employee compensation still compete for it.

blocks.heading: What has Keysight Technologies guided for the year?

paragraphs.text: Keysight’s weighted path is below today’s price, hinging on orders converting into deliveries, margins normalizing, and acquisitions producing cash. Management’s FY2026 guide calls for 32% revenue growth and about 60% EPS growth at the midpoint. For the October 2026 quarter, it guides to $1,930–$1,950 million of revenue and $3.34–$3.40 of non-GAAP EPS, adjusted to exclude costs management treats as outside normal operations. It expects $100 million of cost synergies exiting FY2026.

“Run-rate” savings mean the annual pace expected after the changes are in place, not necessarily the cash saved during the whole year. The table shows management’s current promises for revenue, earnings, acquisitions, synergies, investment, and benefit-plan contributions.

blocks.heading: What do the last eight quarters show for Keysight Technologies?

paragraphs.text: Profit and cash improved with the operating recovery. Gross margin, operating income, net income, and free cash flow all strengthened from the prior-year quarter. But the earnings comparison also benefits from a weak prior-year base and changing tax effects. The improvement is more convincing in revenue, margins, orders, and cash together than in EPS alone.
